St Nicholas School Vision
Our school motto is ‘Shining Together – Embracing our Differences’ as this encompasses the collaborative approach to helping our special pupils achieve their full potential, regardless of their ability. The children at St Nicholas are given daily learning experiences than enable them to be equipped with the skills, knowledge, resilience and life experiences to becomes healthy, active and respectful learners.
Through our Whole School Pathway Model and curriculum, we encourage our pupils to:
Communicate and express their wants and needs
Understand and manage their self-care routine
Express themselves creatively through different experiences
St Nicholas School Ethos:
St Nicholas School prides itself on its child centred approach. Children always come first and the staff at St Nicholas work hard to build up strong relationships with the children and their families.
The staff know each individual child, how they best learn and what support they need. We are empathetic to their needs. Communication is key and we pride ourselves on the relationships we have with parents/carers and the wider professional teams around the children.
The school community work collaboratively; there are shared values. We are supportive of each other, our pupils and their families. Staff are committed professionals; they share knowledge and expertise, and provide a well-resourced, multi-sensory approach in all lessons.
We provide a warm and welcoming place of learning for our pupils where they feel respected, nurtured and safe. Children are encouraged and supported to self-regulate and have a voice to enable them to feel happy, positive and calm in all areas of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Head – St Nicholas School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the St Nicholas School website
St Nicholas School is a good school that caters for pupils with a wide range of special educational needs in the wonderfully diverse borough of Croydon and some from neighbouring boroughs if their SEN needs cannot be met locally. We pride ourselves on being a popular choice with parents who want their child to learn in a safe, supportive and inquisitive environment. We have 225 students on roll who have moderate learning difficulties, communication needs and autism. All children have an Educational Health and Care Plan.
Our school motto is ‘Learning Together’ as this encompasses the collaborative approach to helping our special pupils achieve their full potential, regardless of their ability. The children at St Nicholas are given daily learning experiences that enable them to be equipped with the skills, resilience and life experiences to become healthy, active and respectful learners.
Staff, parents and governors facilitate this by being knowledgeable and confident themselves in a wide range of strategies and pedagogy that support our varied learners.
I hope you enjoy looking around our website and finding out more about our wonderful school. We do hold open mornings throughout the year and encourage you to come along and see the amazing work that we are doing.
Read about our school's ethos and values here.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Opening Hours – St Nicholas School
pageCache.text:
Children arrive at school at 8:40am and leave the school at 3:00pm.
We start putting children onto their buses and taxis from 2:45pm so that this done as safely and as calmly as possible.
On the last day of term at Christmas, Easter and Summer, children finish at 1:30pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rights Respecting School – St Nicholas School
pageCache.text:
What is a Rights Respecting School?
The UNICEF Rights Respecting Schools Award (RRSA) is based on principles of equality, dignity, respect, non-discrimination and participation.
The RRSA seeks to put the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child at the heart of a school’s ethos and culture to improve well-being and develop every child’s talents and abilities to their full potential. A rights respecting school is a community where children’s rights are learned, taught, practised, respected, protected and promoted.
Children’s rights are central to all aspects of UNICEF’S, including education, and we use UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
as a framework for our activities. This sets out the rights of every person under 18 and how those rights should be met.

The school aims to be a centre of excellence, offering quality education to pupils and expertise and support to other schools. The curriculum is modified and differentiated to enable each pupil to access the National Curriculum in an appropriate and meaningful way. St Nicholas operates a policy of inclusion ensuring that all pupils receive a broad, balanced and enriched curriculum. The school aims to develop the whole child intellectually, socially, physically and culturally.
Within an atmosphere of trust and security the children are helped to develop confidence and self esteem and are encouraged to be responsible, independent and to develop an awareness of moral and cultural values and a capacity for enjoyment.
